rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: CHAP. LXVI. If his Excellency Robert Earl of Essex ... Reading
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Chapter LXVI concerns whether Essex would take Reading during a siege.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Starts at top of PDF435/printed401; separate from previous Chapter LXV Waller/Hopton figure.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: should take Reading having then surrounded it with his armie
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The text presents an existing siege, not an unbounded future campaign question.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: The historical observer favored one side; question and outcome are not blind.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: his Excellency Robert Earle of Essex
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The querent's named subject was Parliamentarian general Robert Earl of Essex.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Preserve original speaker and political allegiance; not a personal natal horoscope.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: original 1647 printed square twelve-house chart
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The source contains a square horary with planets and house cusps, not a modern ephemeris export.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Original image is authoritative, no independently reproduced geometry.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The original figure prints 17 April 1643, 6:50 PM.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Distinct from the later surrender sentence, which literally prints 27 April 1644.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Dñs diei Moon; hor: Sun
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The central caption gives Moon as ruler of the day and Sun as hour ruler.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Original Latin shorthand and planet glyphs preserved, not overinterpreted.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: A vac: ad sextile Mars et trine Sun
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The figure announces upcoming aspects of Moon to Mars and Sun.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: A prior void-of-course state and the exact sequence require source-native interpretation.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Essex signified by Mars Lord of Scorpio rising
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly assigns Mars, lord of Scorpio on the ascendant, to the Earl of Essex.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Mars's chart conditions carry separate fortune and debility qualifiers.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: His Majesty by Sun Lord of tenth
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Sun as ruler of tenth is assigned to King Charles I.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: His Majesty is not equated with the besieged place.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: relieving forces Venus Pisces and Sun Taurus
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Venus in Pisces and Sun in Taurus are said to represent troops intending to hinder Essex.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Original source offers multiple factors for relief; do not collapse into Sun alone.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Town of Reading by Aquarius fourth
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Aquarius on the fourth house represents Reading.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Distinguish city sign from governor and supply-house roles.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Sir Arthur Aston Saturn lord of fourth
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Governor Sir Arthur Aston is signified by Saturn as fourth lord.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Alleged wounds and later treatment appear elsewhere as author report.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: ammunition and provision by Jupiter lord fifth
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Jupiter, ruler of the fifth, signifies supplies/provisions available in the town.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Historical house role only; no actionable military provisioning method.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Venus locally therein
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Venus physically in the fifth house is also cited for the town's supplies.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Position and interpretive conclusion are distinct assertions.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Mars excellently fortified, except being in his Fall
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Mars is judged very well fortified, with the important exception of fall.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Original sentence explicitly identifies the debility; do not call Mars unconditionally dignified.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: general significator of Warre friendly to querent
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The author treats Mars as the general war significator favorable to his preferred side.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Period authorial framework only; not a validated victory indicator.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Moon separated a vacuo and then applied sextile Mars
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: A previous Moon void condition and subsequent application to Mars are described.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: The text says the time of actual acquisition was unlikely while Moon was void; keep that temporal distinction.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Signes of long ascensions aspect equivalent square
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly describes the sextile by zodiacal aspect as behaving like a square because of long ascension signs.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Do not turn all sextiles into square or drop this exact circumstance.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: much difficulty and some fighting ere he could get it
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The author expects substantial difficulty and combat before Reading could fall.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Historical forecast with no independent prospective sealed record.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Mars and Moon in Reception
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Mars and Moon are described in mutual reception, with Mars in Moon's house.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Maintain reception's direction and stated conditions.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Moon in Mars Terms and Face
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon is said to occupy Mars's terms and face, a condition supporting the forecast.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: No independent dignity-table calculation or exact orb supplied.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: near Cor Leonis, placed also in tenth
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The author cites proximity to the star Cor Leonis and placement in tenth-house context.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: The exact grammatical referent of the phrase is difficult to resolve; do not force an ephemeris position.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: should obtaine and take Reading, and get glory and honour
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly predicts that Essex will eventually take Reading with honor.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: The source describes a preferred outcome; independent case verification belongs in a separate evidence lane.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Sun Majesty significator seventh in fixed Sign
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Sun in the seventh and a fixed sign represents the King's opposition.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Source also characterizes the sign's resistance as sustained.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Majesty would oppose and send Forces relieve Town
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly reports judging that the King would oppose Essex energetically and send relief.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: This forecast does not itself establish the chronology of external military events.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: but should not prevaile Mars better fortified
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He expects the King's relief effort not to prevail because Mars is more fortified than Sun.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Comparative strength remains authorial, not calculated winning probability.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Aquarius sign fourth not afflicted
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says Reading's fourth-house Aquarius was un-afflicted.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: This is a condition supporting the opposing town's strength, not favor for Essex.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Town strong and capable holding out
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He initially judges Reading able to hold out.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Must retain alongside later fall forecast, not collapse all conditions to easy capture.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Venus fifth ... wanted not Ammunition
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Venus in fifth is interpreted as indicating sufficient ammunition.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Source does not independently inventory stores; military claims are documentary only.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Saturn lord fourth in his Fall with South Node
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Governor Aston's significator Saturn is said to be in fall with the lunar south node.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Source-native symbolic reading; glyph and ephemeris parity not independently established.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Mercury and Jupiter not far from South Node
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The author additionally groups Mercury and Jupiter as close to the node.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Nearness undefined, no independently calibrated orb.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Mars with square beholding Saturn
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Mars is said to aspect Saturn by square.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Keep this square distinct from Moon's differently qualified sextile.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: most assured way occasion surrender
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly identifies a way he believed surrender would be induced despite town strength.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: This is an author-reported historical interpretation, not present-day operational advice.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: division amongst principall Officers
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He conjectures that disagreement among principal officers would lead to surrender.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: A period-specific account involving personnel and factional relations; no independent causal identification.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: about eight days from Question Essex Master of Town
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly states a forecast that Essex would control Reading approximately eight days after the query.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Exact outcome (negotiations versus delivery of town) must not be interchanged.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: rather by composition then blood
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He expects surrender by negotiated terms rather than bloodshed.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: There was already substantial fighting; this refers to the mode of transfer.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Sun and Mars separated sextile; Mars from dexter square Saturn
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Two separating aspects are invoked as support for settlement.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Sun–Mars and Mars–Saturn relationships are separately described; avoid collapsing sign types.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Moon direct sextile of Lord of ascendant without frustration
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon's uninterrupted application to the ascendant lord is cited as another reason for eventual capture.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Source says without frustration or prohibition; not a universal sextile guarantee.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Town delivered for Parliaments use 27th April 1644
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The 1647 text literally prints Reading's surrender as 27 April 1644.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: This differs from the figure's April 1643; independent dated accounts identify surrender on 27 April 1643. Retain original 1644 as printed.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: three dayes after time limited by me expired
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly explicitly admits the town's surrender came three days after his forecast deadline.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Treat as a timing miss of final surrender, not an accurate eight-day surrender forecast.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: very Monday before being eight days after Figure they began to treat
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The text distinguishes earlier surrender negotiations, which it places about eight days after the figure.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Negotiations beginning around the prediction date do not equate to actual surrender by that date.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: 17 Apr 1643 figure versus printed 27 Apr 1644 surrender
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The chart and surrender sentences carry visibly conflicting original years.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: A later historical interpretation favors an original typographic error, not permission to alter the original source field.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: King in person came, beaten back at Caversham bridge
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly narrates a Royalist relief attempt involving the King that was repulsed near Caversham Bridge.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Original page provides no independent battle report, although separate historical sources corroborate the 1643 episode.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Sir Arthur Aston hurt in the head
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He reports Governor Aston being injured in the head.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Historical timing and cause require external evidence; not proved by astrological glyph.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: not want ammunition as Venus fifth signifies
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The author says Reading did not lack ammunition and retrospectively aligns this with Venus in fifth.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: This may conflict with some independent accounts of supply pressure; independently adjudicate before calling it correct.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: delivered by Colonel Fielding
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He attributes the town's surrender to Colonel Feilding/Fielding.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Retain spelling and role; neither validates an astrological forecast.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Colonel Fielding very valiant Gentleman
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly praises Colonel Fielding's character and military service.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: An author's judgment, not a modern biographical finding.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: jealousie and mistrust by King's party underhand dealing
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He reports accusations against Feilding of secret dealings.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Preserve accusations as contested and unproven; never factual guilt attribution.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: trouble but evaded
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He reports Fielding getting into difficulty but avoiding severe sanction.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Historical court-martial/response should be corroborated independently.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: royalist officers believed Fielding acted honourably
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says some Royalist officers defended Fielding as acting honorably.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: This is third-party hearsay within Lilly's own account.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: person of honour demanded Question, satisfied
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The author says an honorable questioner was satisfied by the reading.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: User satisfaction reported by author is not independent test of forecast.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Had this very Question been of a Law-suit
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly explicitly reuses the siege figure hypothetically for a legal dispute.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: It is an unnumbered analogy within LXVI; not a new numbered chapter.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: ascendant lord and Moon querent or Plaintiff
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: In a lawsuit framing, the first-house lord, ascendant and Moon represent the plaintiff.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Distinct from actual battle meanings; avoid mixing with physical military outcome.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: seventh and its lord Defendant
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The seventh and its lord represent the opposing defendant.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Legal role is source-native analogical mapping, not a verified litigation case.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Moon applying sextile Mars verdict of Jurors for Plaintiff
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says the plaintiff would receive a favorable jury verdict from the Moon's application.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: A counterfactual legal prediction without an observed court case.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Sun seventh and tenth lord signifies Judge
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He assigns Sun as the judge significator because it rules the tenth while placed in seventh.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Keep tenth-house ruler and seventh-house placement separate.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Judge adverse to Plaintiff
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly expects a judge hostile to the plaintiff, aligned with the King against Essex.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: This is a hypothetical legal judgment, not a verified court ruling.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Venus Lady eighth (defendant second) in exaltation
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly uses an exalted Venus, ruler of the plaintiff's eighth and opponent's derived second, to argue defendant's wealth.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: The legal section derives houses relative to parties; not a real financial judgment.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Defendant able to spend well
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He predicts the hypothetical defendant could afford considerable litigation costs.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Unobserved law-suit hypothetical, not historical evidence.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Sun and Mars sextile
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: A sextile between Sun and Mars is used in discussing judicial settlement.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Need retain two significators and exact aspect type.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Judge would labour to compound matter betwixt both
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He proposes the judge would seek to reconcile the disputants.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Hypothetical legal prediction rather than observed settlement.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Dispositor of Part Fortune Saturn in Aries in Fall with South Node
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly locates Saturn in fall in Aries with the lunar South Node.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: This is the original written astrological premise; independent glyph/ephemeris check pending.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: great expense of Plaintiff estate and money
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He predicts the plaintiff's lawsuit would consume substantial money.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Period source statement about a hypothetical case, not factual lawsuit costs.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Saturn and Mars square
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: An alleged Saturn-Mars square is interpreted as an adversarial indicator.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Keep angular aspect, no independent mathematical comparison.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Saturn great enemy to plaintiff
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Saturn is assigned as a third party hostile to the hypothetical plaintiff.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Cannot accuse any historical or living person on this basis.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Saturn Lord third
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Saturn is named ruler of third house in this counterfactual lawsuit framing.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Original house-ruler relationship preserved even when analogical.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: ill neighbour or Brother or Kinsman
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly lists neighbor, brother or male relation as possible people causing trouble.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Alternatives, not a unique identifying diagnostic.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: third house ninth from seventh, priest or sister's husband
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He suggests a priest or the defendant's sister's husband could be involved under derived-house interpretation.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Keep these distinct alternative symbolic referents.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: Plaintiff take such offer or compound
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says the imaginary plaintiff should consider compromise in the hypothetical dispute.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: This is an author's period judicial judgment, not contemporary legal advice.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: if his Enemy's Attorney Saturnine, rigour causes prejudice
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He conjectures a Saturnine opposing attorney could cause harm through rigid prosecution.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Printed sentence crosses original PDF437–438; unverified personality/intent claims.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: if Saturn signify his Lawyer damage by him
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: An alternative reading identifies Saturn as one's own lawyer who causes harm.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Preserve changed symbolic referent; do not equate with the opposing attorney.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: perhaps aged man Father Grandfather or sturdy Tenant
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The author offers an elderly relation, father, grandfather, hostile tenant or similar person as further possible referents.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Mutually competing figurations, not predictions identifying real people.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: according to nature of Question vary the rules
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He concludes the exact original question determines which of these analogies is relevant.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Do not transform this permissive interpretive flexibility into a frozen objective classifier.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: knowledge of question to attaine perfection of Art
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly emphasizes contextual knowledge as necessary to interpretation.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Retrospective flexibility undermines mechanical blind predictive transfer; document it rather than silently resolving.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: The eight House ... Of Death, Dowry ... CHAP. LXVII
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: A decorative divider separates LXVI from the eighth-house section and Chapter LXVII.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Navigation-only marker. The new eighth-house introduction and Chapter LXVII body are NOT LXVI source units.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_full_quote: If absent party be alive or dead?
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The next numbered question concerns whether an absent person is alive.
rows.qualifications_ambiguity_scope: Chapter LXVII begins below divider on original PDF438/printed404, outside Chapter LXVI.
